PP1 · Chapter 1 of 6

Count with me

Touch each object once, then connect a small group to its number.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

By the end I can…

  • I can count a small group.
  • I can match a group to a number.
  • I can find the next number.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Touch and count

Touch each apple once.

Say a number for each touch.

1, 2, 3. There are 3 apples.

Screen 2 of 4

The last number says how many

Count the balls: 1, 2, 3, 4.

The last number you say is how many.

There are 4 balls.

Screen 3 of 4

Match the group to its number

Here are 5 counters.

Count them. Say 5.

The number 5 matches this group.

Screen 4 of 4

What comes next?

Numbers go in order.

After 4 comes 5.

Hop one step to find the next number.

Words to know
count
Say one number for each thing you touch.
how many
The last number you say tells how many.
next
The number that comes after.

For parents

What your child learns

Your child learns to touch each thing once and say one number for each. The last number said tells how many. This is the base of all later number work.

A common slip

Counting a thing twice or skipping one. Slide each object across as it is counted, so every one gets exactly one number.

5-minute home activity: Count the snack

  1. Put up to 5 raisins or grapes on a plate.
  2. Let your child touch and move each one while counting aloud.
  3. Ask, "How many are there?" and listen for the last number.
  4. Add one more. Ask what number comes next.
